### `cloud eval create`

Create a runnable eval suite from authored test cases (does not run it).

| Flag | Require
d | Description |\n| - | - | - |\n| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently updated proj
ect) |\n| `--file <path>` | No | Path to a **create-API JSON** body (or `-` for stdin). A versioned suite file (`schemaVersion: \"
1\"`) belongs on `eval run --file` |\n| `--json <json>` | No | Inline suite definition JSON (or `@file`, or `-` for stdin) |\n| `-
-name <name>` | No | Suite name (overrides the file) |\n| `--model <model>` | No | Suite-level default model (overrides the file)
|\n| `--provider <provider>` | No | Suite-level default provider (overrides the file) |\n| `--server <id-or-name...>` | No | Proje
ct HTTP server names or IDs (overrides the file) |\n| `--client <id-or-name...>` | No | Clients to attach the suite to (overrides
the file). Without one the suite lists no client, and `eval run --client` has nothing to select |\n| `--host <id-or-name...>` | No

| **Deprecated** alias for `--client`. Passing both is an error. |

### `cloud eval list`

List the eval suites saved in a pr

oject.

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to the

most recently updated project) |

### `cloud eval run`

Start an eval run of an existing suite, or upload a versioned suite fi
le and run it. Provide **either** `--suite` **or** `--file`, not both.\n\nBy default the command prints a launch receipt and retur
ns immediately. `--wait` polls every launched run to a terminal state.\n\n**Exit codes (`--wait` only).** Without `--wait` this co
mmand's exit code is unchanged: `0` on any launch, `1` on a partial or wholly failed fan-out. `--wait` owns a separate six-code co
ntract — a caller who asked this process to sit and watch a run to completion is asking it to say how the run went:\n\n| Code | Me

aning |
| - | - |
| `0` | Every waited run passed, unanimously, and (when a report was requested) every report was assembled |
| `1` | A run **completed** with a **failed** verdict. The only condition that produces this code |\n| `2` | Usage error — bad fla
gs, `--reporter`/`--out` without `--wait`, or an invalid suite file (after auth, before any server/model work) |\n| `3` | Auth fai
led — no credential, or the platform rejected it, at launch or mid-wait (a token that expired during a long poll). Zero credits sp
ent if it happened before launch |\n| `4` | Connection/setup failed before evaluation — a launch failure this CLI itself observed
(network, timeout, rate limit, a partial or failed fan-out, an unrecognized launch error), or a local `--out` write failure — unle
ss a more severe outcome (`1` or `3`) already applies to the same run, per the merge order above |\n| `5` | No valid verdict — `in
conclusive`, a null/unrecognized result, a run whose own status is failed/cancelled/timed-out, a wait that hit its deadline, a mid
-wait failure that was not auth-shaped, or a report that could not be assembled |\n\nNo infrastructure condition ever maps to `1`
— see the same rule under `eval gate` below. A multi-target launch merges these worst-of across every waited run, in the order `1
> 3 > 4 > 5 > 0`: a real verdict failure is never masked by a sibling's infrastructure noise, and a credential failure (which may
be *why* other targets show no verdict) outranks a plain connection failure.\n\nThis six-code contract is new and deliberately **d
ifferent** from `eval gate`'s four codes below — see that command's own doc for why the two are not unified. An invalid suite file
exits **2** either way — `eval validate` still exits 1 for the same contract failure, because it is a verdict on the file and thi

s command is not.

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--suite <id-or-name>` | Yes, unless `--file` | Eval suit
e name or ID |\n| `--file <path>` | Yes, unless `--suite` | Versioned suite file to upload and run (`.yaml` or `.json`, or `-` for
stdin) |\n| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently updated project) |\n| `--server <id
-or-name...>` | No | Override the suite's saved server selection (HTTP servers only) |\n| `--environment <id-or-name...>` | No | A
ttached project environment(s) to run. Several values start one **paid run each**. |\n| `--client <id-or-name...>` | No | Attached
client(s) to run, so the run is stamped with that client's config. Several values start one **paid run each**. |\n| `--host <id-o
r-name...>` | No | **Deprecated** alias for `--client`. Passing both is an error. Not the host-compat catalog id `mcpjam compat --
host` / `mcpjam tools --host` take — see [Two different `--host` flags](#two-different---host-flags). |\n| `--all-targets` | No |
Run **every** attached environment (or, if none, every attached host) — one **paid run per target** |\n| `--iterations <n>` | No |
Run each case this many times (1-10), for this run only |\n| `--repetitions <n>` | No | **Legacy** spelling of `--iterations`. Pa
ssing both is an error. |\n| `--case <id-or-title...>` | No | Run only these cases instead of the whole suite |\n| `--exclude-skil
ls` | No | Run the \"without skills\" A/B arm: nothing is pinned, and the run is labelled as excluded |\n| `--refresh-snapshot` |
No | **Persists a new host-config snapshot on the suite** (see below). Single-target runs only. |\n| `--notes <text>` | No | Free-
text note stored on the run |\n| `--min-pass-rate <n>` | No | Pass threshold for this run (0-100), overriding the suite's own |\n|
`--match-options <json>` | No | Tool-call match options for this run, e.g. `'{\"toolCallOrder\":\"exact\"}'` |\n| `--idempotency-
key <key>` | No | Retry key for a lost launch response. For `--file`, a fresh key is minted and printed on every invocation when t
his flag is omitted; supply the printed key to replay the same run instead of starting a new one |\n| `--wait` | No | Wait for eve
ry launched run to reach a terminal status |\n| `--wait-timeout <ms>` | No | Maximum wait time (default 2100000); requires `--wait
` |\n| `--reporter <json-summary\\|junit-xml\\|html>` | No | Write the completed structured report to stdout; requires `--wait`. `
html` is a self-contained decision summary + failures page — traces/parity/history are not included. |\n| `--out <path>` | No | At
omically write the completed report to a file; defaults to `json-summary`, or uses `--reporter` when present; requires `--wait` |\
n| `--compose-client <id-or-name>` | No | Compose a stack to run instead of naming a saved environment (see below). **Ephemeral by
default** — pass `--save-targets` to attach it to the suite. |\n| `--compose-host <id-or-name>` | No | **Deprecated** alias for `
--compose-client` |\n| `--compose-computer <id-or-name>` | No | Sandbox image to pin on the composed stack |\n| `--compose-model <
id...>` | No | Model(s) to run on the composed stack. Replaces the client's pinned model unless `--with-client-default` is set |\n
| `--compose-model-selection <json...>` | No | Whole saved model selection(s) — source, connection, `settings.reasoningEffort` — a
s JSON: one cell per selection, for its model, at its effort. Repeat to add several selections for one model (e.g. at low and at h
igh) — each distinct selection is its own cell |\n| `--with-client-default` | No | Also launch an inherit cell using each client's
pinned model, alongside `--compose-model` |\n| `--compose-server <id-or-name...>` | No | Server(s) to pin on the composed stack,
snapshotted into a server group so a rerun keeps testing them. Mutually exclusive with `--compose-server-group` |\n| `--compose-se
rver-group <id>` | No | Standalone server group to pin on the composed stack |\n| `--compose-host-servers` | No | **No longer supp
orted** — rejected. An eval run takes its servers from a server group alone; use `--compose-server` or `--compose-server-group` |\
